newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.

Indonesia's three sanctioned political parties submitted their candidates lists for next year's general elections. Golkar, the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and the United Development Party (PPP) submitted a total of 2,603 candidates for the 425 seats in the national parliament. A list submitted by ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri's faction was not accepted by electoral officials.

Australian Prime Minister John Howard began a three-day official visit by saying at a state dinner that he hoped that the relationship between the two countries would not be spoilt by political and cultural differences.
Indonesia's national carrier Garuda has recorded first half losses of 2.65 billion rupiah ($1.14 million). Garuda is expected to list its shares on the capital market in 1998.
Transport minister Haryanto Dhanutirto said that illegal fishing in the waters off Indonesia was not his ministry's responsibility.
Indonesia is expected to offer non-fiscal incentives for companies to boost economic growth in the provinces which are part of the ASEAN economic growth area.
